research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding PNR (sequential action pair)
derived play-type labels from play-by-play (proxy-calibrated PNR, DRIVE)
methodological_questions: Can DRIVE and PNR be labeled reliably enough from play-by-play to define the sequence and the outcome?
Does a drive-then-PNR sequence raise PNR PPP beyond player, lineup, opponent and game-state confounding?
Is the PNR PPP outcome mechanically tied to the label construction (foul endings, proxy calibration)?
Is there enough drive-then-PNR exposure per cell for a powered test?
Does an effect survive placebo or ordering falsification (e.g. drive following PNR, drive to other play types)?

historical_evidence.finding: Season stability of teammate X->Y sequence premiums: only 2/30 stars had a stable top suppressor. Some negative sequences were listed, including Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 (n=31) and Tatum->Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444 (n=31). Cells had min n=20 and the family carries a SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risk.

Play-type label backfill verification across 921,514 possessions: PNR share 28.7% (band 20-28%) FAIL, PULL_UP FAIL, 3100 games with team PNR >33%, team identity FAIL; PNR PPP 0.948 PASS; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. Final: FAIL.

Label accuracy audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw rate 1.7% vs 14-22% benchmark, most play-type PPPs above benchmark band; foul possessions leak into OTHER. Recorded mechanism: C_artifact.

Labeling audit: DRIVE 12pp below foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK), PNR shows a 22% foul rate, OTHER PPP inflated by 36% foul endings; only 0.7% of 50,668 possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type.

2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots ranges from OKC 7.567% to IND 13.824%; these rates served as calibration input for the PBPProxyPNR label, with later logs showing calibrated PNR ~17.9-19.6% of possessions. No pass/fail gate.
On-ball coverage labels from matchup/PBP fields reached only 14.9% and 3.3% confident label rates; switches_on was unpopulated; verdict failed_gate.

Adaptation falsification: the apparent PPP lift failed asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests, with wrong-way teams not doing worse than no-signal teams. Risks recorded: LABEL_ERROR, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, selection or regression to the mean.
Star suppression by lineup and forced play type was descriptive only; no placebo or matching, and later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.why: Distribution and team-identity checks failed; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy-calibrated (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels (DRIVE, OTHER) as measurement instruments
failed_approaches.why: Label audit failed; DRIVE foul rate was far below benchmark and foul possessions leaked into OTHER (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating play-type PPP differences as real efficiency
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending labeling artifacts inflated or deflated PPP; PNR itself shows a 22% foul rate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Finding stable teammate X->Y sequence premiums, including DRIVE->PNR
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null for stability (B_powered_null); cells of ~20-31 possessions.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball coverage from matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Very low confident-label rate; switches_on not populated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading a PPP lift as a real response without falsification
failed_approaches.why: Falsification tests (asymmetry, confidence dose-response, carryover) failed; recorded as artifact.

evidence_establishes: Per the records, the derived PNR and DRIVE labels have failed audits (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025), with foul-ending leakage and heavy proxy calibration of PNR labels.

Earlier work on teammate DRIVE->PNR sequence premiums found small cells (n~31) and no season-stable sequence effects (FAM:SF-APPA-058); one DRIVE->PNR cell (Giannis->Lillard) showed a negative gap, which is directionally opposite to the hypothesis but not a test of it.
Earlier descriptive sequence gaps were treated as artifacts when lacking placebo or matching (FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-001).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record directly tests whether any teammate drive preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP in a pooled, controlled analysis.
The records do not show that a corrected labeling pipeline (foul handling, non-proxy PNR identification) would fail or pass.
They do not give the number of drive-then-PNR sequences available per season or the variance of PNR PPP at sequence level.
own_inferences: 'Any teammate DRIVE' pools heterogeneous drives (rim attacks, kick-outs, failed drives) and so is vaguely specified; the hypothesis needs an operational window and a drive definition (e.g. drive within N seconds and same possession, with the PNR ball handler differing from the driver).

Because both the drive and PNR labels are proxy-derived from the same possession stream, a sequence labeled 'drive then PNR' is likely to be selected by possession length, shot clock state, and non-foul outcomes, creating a mechanical association with PPP independent of any causal effect.

The sign is ambiguous: a drive followed by a PNR implies the possession already reset/extended with less shot clock, which may lower PPP, while defensive rotation after a drive might raise it; a one-sided 'raises' prediction is not well founded.
The directional hint from the negative DRIVE->PNR cell, combined with the prior artifact record, makes a naive positive effect unlikely to survive.
uncertainties: Whether the per-game play-by-play contains enough explicit drive events (action sub-types) to define DRIVE directly without the proxy label.
Whether PNR can be identified from anything other than the proxy calibration (screen assists, screener events), and whether the 2025-26 partial data change this.
The retrieval result truncates some records (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPA-001); full text was not read and no follow-up tool was used.
Opposing defensive scheme is essentially unlabelable (FAM:SF-APPS-058), so coverage confounding cannot be controlled directly.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history this would be a straightforward proceed-style observational comparison. The retrieved records show that the labels underlying both the exposure and the outcome failed audits with foul leakage and proxy calibration, that earlier sequence-premium work had small cells and was treated as artifact-prone, and that unfalsified PPP lifts were artifacts. This moved the decision to proceed_with_changes: a restricted, pre-registered design using event-level definitions, foul-inclusive PPP, a placebo, and gates.

blocking_constraints.text: DRIVE and PNR labels failed prior audits; a sequence defined from them inherits error and the PNR is largely proxy-calibrated.
PNR PPP and the labels are derived from the same possession outcomes, with foul endings leaking across play-type buckets.
Ball-handler quality, lineup, opponent defense, shot-clock state and possession length are tied to both drive occurrence and PNR PPP, and defensive scheme is not labelable.

prior_work.summary: No record tests the pooled question. Related work on star-level DRIVE->PNR sequence premiums found small unstable cells (rejected for stability), and label audits showed both play types are unreliable instruments. The question is therefore not answered, but earlier results argue against trusting a naive test.

risks.text: Failed label audits for DRIVE and PNR; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated.
Play-type and PPP are both derived from the possession; foul endings are misallocated across types.
Player quality, lineup, opponent, game state and clock; team style (drive-heavy teams also run more PNR).
If the PNR label is assigned using the possession outcome or later events, exposure or label depends on the future; the drive-then-PNR window must use only information preceding the PNR.
Drive-then-PNR sequences within a possession are probably rare; prior sequence cells had n~20-31.
Per-player or per-pair splits will be underpowered; PPP has SD around 1.1-1.2 per possession.
Possessions that include a prior action are longer and may have shot-clock constraints and fewer turnovers/early shots, creating a built-in PPP difference.
Splitting by driver, handler, season or window multiplies tests; only one primary contrast is allowed.
Label pipeline and league tendencies may differ across 2022-23 to 2025-26; 2025-26 is partial.
Without a placebo (e.g. a drive following a PNR, or a non-PNR action) the association cannot be distinguished from possession-structure effects.

design.estimand: Within-possession difference in points per possession (including free throws and fouls, and turnovers as zero) on PNR possessions where a teammate of the PNR ball handler had a DRIVE event in the same possession within the preceding K seconds (K pre-registered, default 8 s), versus PNR possessions with no such preceding drive, adjusted for handler, lineup, opponent and game state. Secondary: effect on the possession-level shot quality (shot distance, result) as a mechanism check.
design.unit: Half-court possession containing an identified PNR. Clusters: game and offensive team-season.
design.sample: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs as the exploratory set (labeled-pipeline development only) and a locked confirmatory set: 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete (2026-06-21). Exclude possessions with fewer than 8 s left on the shot clock at PNR start, garbage time, and heave/end-of-period possessions. Define DRIVE from explicit play-by-play event sub-types rather than the proxy label and require the driver to be a different player than the PNR ball handler; define PNR from screen/handler events where available and report the share that is proxy-calibrated, and fall back to a high-confidence subset only.
design.power: Compute before analysis from the observed count of eligible sequences. Assuming PPP SD ~1.15 and a minimum effect of interest of +0.05 PPP, a two-group comparison needs roughly 4,200 exposed possessions at 80% power (alpha 0.05 two-sided) before design effect; with clustering inflate by about 1.2-1.5. If exposed possessions in the confirmatory season are below this, report as underpowered/untestable rather than inferring a null; pooling seasons only for the equivalence/null judgement.
design.controls: Fixed effects for PNR ball handler, screener, opponent team, offensive lineup or team-season, period, score margin bucket, shot clock at PNR start, and possession start type (off make, miss, turnover); include the driver's identity as a random effect; adjust for time since possession start. Use matching or coarsened exact matching on handler x possession start x shot-clock-at-PNR as a robustness check. Foul endings counted in PPP for all conditions.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: replace 'preceding drive' with a drive that occurs after the PNR, or with a preceding non-drive action (e.g. a pass or handoff); a similar estimated effect implies a possession-structure artifact. (2) Label gate: on a hand-audited sample of at least 200 sequences, require DRIVE and PNR label precision >= 0.80, else the result is classified untestable. (3) Foul-leakage check: repeat excluding foul-ending possessions and with all fouls counted. (4) Dose-response by K window and number of preceding drives; a real effect should be monotone or at least stable. (5) Exploratory-set estimate must have the same sign as the confirmatory one.
design.multiplicity: One primary confirmatory contrast (all qualifying drive-then-PNR vs none, season 2025-26 regular season). All other splits (by driver type, handler, season, window) are labeled exploratory and Holm-adjusted across at most 6 pre-listed secondary contrasts.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary adjusted effect is >= +0.05 PPP with the 95% cluster-robust CI excluding 0, the placebo effect is <= half the primary effect and not significant, the label gate is passed, and the sign is replicated in the exploratory seasons. Rejected if power was sufficient and the 95% CI excludes +0.05 (equivalence bound). Untestable if the label gate fails or exposed possessions are below the power requirement. Artifact if the primary effect is present but the placebo effect is comparable or it disappears after foul-leakage and shot-clock controls.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play and rotation files for 2022-23 through 2025-26 as of 2026-06-14, with the derived play-type possession graph used only for possession boundaries; freeze the extraction and code hash before confirmatory runs; 2025-26 playoffs excluded as incomplete.

methodological_questions: Does a teammate drive immediately before a PNR raise PNR PPP?
How reliable is the derived play-type label for drives and PNRs from play-by-play?
Is the PNR outcome label derived from the same possession outcome, creating circularity or leakage?
Confounding by player quality, lineup, opponent defense and game context
Sample size and exposure sparsity of drive-then-PNR sequences
args.query: Does any teammate drive preceding a pick-and-roll raise PNR points per possession, and what data-quality and play-type labeling issues affect testing it?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
